questions.question: Describe your experience testing Navy systems for Naval Target Control and the Navy Command Datalink Program. How did you translate software requirements into test scripts and traceability evidence?
You have programmed in C#, Visual Basic, and C++. Can you walk us through a specific C++ or C# component you developed, including its design, testing approach, and how you resolved defects?
This role requires managing multiple Agile sprint teams and release plans. What experience have you had coordinating testing work, release readiness, hot fixes, or competing priorities across a team?
Tell us about the proprietary testing tools you modified at Conduent. What problem did each change address, how did you implement it, and what measurable improvement resulted?
How have you used Jira, Microsoft Test Management, or Team Foundation Server to manage defects, test cases, requirements, and release status?

Describe your experience setting up automated testing for the five stand-alone programs on the JTCG/ME contract. What tools, scripting languages, test coverage, and maintenance practices were involved?
What is your approach to verifying that a defect has been fixed and that the fix has not introduced regressions, particularly for systems with software and hardware dependencies?

This position involves leadership and mentoring of a 15–20 person organization. Drawing on your Army Team Leader role and software teams, how have you organized work, supported teammates, and maintained accountability?
Describe your experience with SQL Server 2014 and relational data. What role did you play in its setup or maintenance, and how did it support the applications or testing environment?

The role supports complex, potentially real-time ITS and connected-vehicle systems. Based on your Navy and classified-system experience, how would you approach developing a test strategy for a safety- or mission-critical system with timing, hardware, and communications dependencies?
